records.title: Aldosterone promotes cardiac endothelial cell proliferation in vivo.
records.model: Seven-day aldosterone-treated mice, human endothelial cells ex vivo, and a transverse-aortic-constriction heart-failure model

recovered_alias_roles.role_evidence: Pharmacological mineralocorticoid-receptor blockade inhibited endothelial proliferation in the transverse-aortic-constriction model.

administered_agents.name: aldosterone
administered_agents.role: Administered to mice for seven days; induces cardiac endothelial proliferation

administered_agents.name: eplerenone
administered_agents.role: Administered receptor antagonist in the heart-failure model; exposure details absent

records.note: Aldosterone increased cardiac endothelial proliferation. In a separate pressure-overload heart-failure model, eplerenone blockade of the mineralocorticoid receptor inhibited endothelial proliferation.
records.uncertainty: The abstract does not provide eplerenone dose, timing, magnitude or cardiac-performance outcomes. Reduced endothelial proliferation is a directional cellular result, not demonstrated heart-failure rescue or evidence for benefit in muscle or BUB1B-associated disease. The seven-day exposure explicitly describes aldosterone, not eplerenone.
records.followup_reason: Resolve the eplerenone dose/timing, species, endothelial endpoint, vascular remodeling and cardiac function before deciding whether proliferation suppression is useful or harmful.
records.new_lead_assessment: New named-drug cellular intervention recovered, and no existing eplerenone decision was found in the checked ledger; qualifies for a narrow primary-source mechanism/direction follow-up, not as a beneficial repurposing lead.
